input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, I found no evidence that would weaken or overturn it:

H1 (Restatements): No evidence was found indicating any restatements or corrections to the prior year quarter (March 29, 2025) net sales figures. The retrieved evidence (E10, E11, E12) discusses tax matters, filing status, and revenue disaggregation, but contains no mention of restatements affecting the comparability of the periods.

H2 (Accounting policy changes): No evidence was found of revenue recognition policy changes between the two periods that would affect comparability. E13 discusses litigation impacts on revenue, E14 discusses privacy compliance, and E15 discusses a new accounting standard (ASU 2025-06) for internal-use software that will be effective in 2029, not affecting the current comparison. E12 shows consistent revenue disaggregation for both periods.

H3 (Acquisitions/divestitures): No evidence was found of acquisitions, divestitures, or discontinued operations affecting the comparability of net sales between the quarters. E16 discusses employee culture, E17 discusses operating expenses and taxes, and E18 discusses purchase obligations and tax payments, but none mention business combinations or discontinued operations affecting revenue comparability.

The evidence review confirms that E7, E8, and E9 (XBRL facts and derived metrics with EXACT_MATCH or COMPATIBLE_AFTER_VERIFIED_DERIVATION period compatibility) ENTAIL the claim, showing net sales grew from $95.359 billion to $111.184 billion (17% or 16.6% growth) for the quarter ended March 28, 2026 versus the prior year quarter. The initial SUPPORTED verdict remains correct.
